india.rationale: Facts: NSE provisional data show FIIs bought a net Rs 45,960cr in cash equities over Nov 2-6, after a net October FPI outflow of about $3.67bn. Sensex had its best week in six years (+8.8%), and the rupee hit 94.06-94.13/USD, its strongest since May. Brent fell from about $118 (Oct 30 futures) to about $94-99, and Iran reportedly exempted Indian ships from Hormuz restrictions. Offsets: October CPI (Nov 12) is expected around 5.9-6.2%, at or above the RBI's 6% ceiling, after the RBI hiked to 5.50% on Oct 7, so a Dec 4 hike is possible. FX reserves are $717bn, about $69bn below the September peak, and part of the rupee's strength comes from RBI tools. OFAC sanctioned an India-based Iran-oil shipping network on Nov 4. The Graham Act Russia-oil tariff waiver (EO 14436) is open-ended but revocable at will; there is no Dec 15 deadline. Interpretation: oil relief and rotation out of North-Asia AI hardware give a mild tailwind, but much of it is already priced after a +8.8% week, and it reverses if a US strike on Iran lifts oil.

em_asia_other.rationale: Facts: Taiwan and Korea crashed in the AI and semiconductor rout that followed the US midterms. TAIEX fell 4.51% to 39,701 on Nov 6 (-12.19% for the week, -20.55% from the Oct 6 high) as foreigners sold a record NT$994bn in October. Taiwan authorised its NT$500bn stabilisation fund and cut short-sale limits from Nov 9. KOSPI fell 6.02% on Nov 6 with a circuit breaker and about 12tn won of foreign selling over six sessions; Korea has so far only waived margin-collateral rules. For Indonesia, MSCI's Oct 15 consultation on demoting it to Standalone keeps a passive-outflow overhang, with a decision due by June 2027. Offsets: TSMC guided Q4 +14% q/q, Korean October chip exports rose 259%, and Indonesia's Q3 GDP grew 5.47% with reserves up to $146.8bn. Interpretation: the shock is US policy and positioning rather than a collapse in demand, so -1 rather than -2. TSMC's October sales (around Nov 10) are the swing factor.

latam.rationale: Facts: Brazil's Copom held the Selic at 13.75% on Nov 4 (7-0), ending its easing cycle, with inflation above the ceiling and a 2026 IPCA projection of 5.6%. The real lost about 8% after Lula's Oct 25 re-election and was at 5.50-5.51/USD on Nov 6, the high for the series. Gross debt is 82.9% of GDP and no fiscal measures have been announced (Lula is due to speak Nov 8). Banxico cut 25bp to 6.25% on a 3-2 vote, called it a one-off and signalled the end of easing as the peso weakened about 5% in October. Copper fell about 5% from late-October highs. Offsets: LatAm was low-beta to the AI crash (Ibovespa -0.82% on Nov 5, +0.29% for the week), the USMCA review cliff is in 2027, and CLP and PEN held stable. Interpretation: Brazil's fiscal premium is the main drag; a credible fiscal message could reverse it.

em_broad.rationale: Facts: Taiwan and Korea, the two largest EM weights after China, are in bear markets with record foreign outflows and weaker currencies (NT$ near 33, won at 1,356.6). HK and China tech fell with the US on Nov 6 despite PBOC and State Council support pledges. Brazil's real weakened about 8% after the election, and Turkey's October CPI beat forecasts at 29.77% with USD/TRY above 50. Offsets: money rotated into India within EM (record FII buying), lower oil helps importers, and South Africa's MTBPS and GDP rebase were credit-positive. Interpretation: in a cap-weighted EM basket the North-Asia AI-hardware drawdown outweighs the rotation, which is a reallocation inside EM rather than net inflow, so this is a mild headwind and the same AI-factor risk as tech_ai_semis, not an independent view.

regime_notes: Two US-driven shocks pulled EM in opposite directions. First, the midterm data-centre backlash and the Microsoft/Oracle/neocloud pullback set off the Nov 5 SOX -12% crash, which hit Korea (circuit breaker) and Taiwan (bear market, stabilisation fund) hardest even though their export data are at records. Second, the political read that the Iran war cost Republicans the election helped knock Brent from about $118 to about $94-99, which favoured importers: India had its best week in six years on record FII buying, and Turkey rallied. This was rotation within EM, not new money, and it is likely to reverse together if semis rebound or a US strike lifts oil. Brazil carries its own post-election fiscal premium, and both Copom and Banxico have stopped easing. Nov 10-12 (TSMC October sales, US CPI, India CPI, the CBRT inflation report) and the FGE mid-November to mid-December Iran strike window are the swing factors.

red_flags.issue: Index change: iShares moves EWY to the MSCI Korea 25/50 Daily 25 Capped index on or around 2026-11-09, so any group entity above 25% is trimmed to 22.5% between rebalances. This is mechanical trimming of Samsung group weight and causes rebalance trades during a volatile market. The ETF priced the Nov 5 US move ahead of the KOSPI (EWY -13.46% that day), but it was at -0.09% to NAV on Nov 6, with no stress discount.

Taiwan market intervention: the NT$500bn stabilisation fund is authorised, short-sale limits are cut to 3% of volume and short margin raised to 130% from Nov 9, and the TAIEX fell as much as 9% intraday on Nov 6. Expect timing gaps between the US-listed ETF and the home market, and wider premiums or discounts.

MSCI consultation (Oct 15) on reclassifying Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone status. MSCI expects to proceed unless governance materially improves, with a decision on or before 2027-06-30. The index freeze and High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) deletions continue. EIDO is small ($384M) and traded at a +0.68% premium on Nov 6.

Lira above 50/USD (USD/TRY 50.158 on Nov 6) after an upside surprise in October CPI (29.77%), a currency-translation drag for USD holders. The 'record low' claim has not been confirmed by a top-tier source.

The Graham Act 100% tariff on major Russian-oil buyers is waived without an expiry date, but the President or Secretary of State can revoke it at any time. A separate OFAC action on Nov 4 sanctioned an India-based Iran-oil shipping network.
